cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If A and B are finite sets with |A|>|B|, then no function from A to B is injective; equivalently, every such function maps two distinct elements of A to the same element of B.
required_concepts: A and B are finite sets with |A|>|B|.
No function from A to B is injective.
Equivalently, every such function has a collision between two distinct inputs.
major_error_concepts: Applying the finite principle to arbitrary infinite subsets without a theorem.

cards.prompt: Define Rational countability construction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The diagonal enumeration of integer numerator and positive denominator pairs followed by duplicate control to cover every rational.
required_concepts: The diagonal enumeration of integer numerator and positive denominator pairs followed by duplicate control to cover every rational.
major_error_concepts: Inferring uncountability because rationals are dense in reals.

cards.prompt: What is the Schroeder-Bernstein theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** Schroeder-Bernstein converts two opposite injections into equality of cardinality without requiring either injection to be inverted; it asserts existence of a bijection rather than identifying it as a composition.
required_concepts: It proves equal cardinality from injections in both directions.
It guarantees a bijection but does not say that either injection or their composition is that bijection.
major_error_concepts: Claiming that the two supplied injections are inverses or that their composition is automatically the promised bijection.

cards.prompt: State the Schroeder-Bernstein theorem, including both hypotheses and its conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If there is an injection from A to B and an injection from B to A, then there is a bijection between A and B.
required_concepts: There is an injection from A to B.
There is an injection from B to A.
Therefore there is a bijection between A and B.
major_error_concepts: Using one injection each way without checking directions or assuming their composition is the required bijection.

cards.term: Subset of a countable set theorem: role
cards.prompt: What is Subset of a countable set theorem used for, and what is its main limitation?
cards.definition: **Theorem role.** It lets countability pass from an ambient set to every subset by restricting or filtering an enumeration, a basic closure property used throughout analysis; a subset may be finite rather than countably infinite.
required_concepts: It lets countability pass from an ambient set to every subset by restricting or filtering an enumeration, a basic closure property used throughout analysis
a subset may be finite rather than countably infinite.
major_error_concepts: Calling the subset countably infinite without proving it is infinite.

cards.term: Subset of a countable set theorem
cards.prompt: State Subset of a countable set theorem, including its hypotheses and conclusion.
cards.definition: **Theorem statement.** If A is countable and B is a subset of A, then B is countable under the convention that finite sets are countable; B need not be countably infinite.
required_concepts: A is countable and B is a subset of A.
Therefore B is countable under the finite-or-countably-infinite convention.
The conclusion does not imply that B is countably infinite.
major_error_concepts: Calling the subset countably infinite without proving it is infinite.

cards.prompt: What must an argument rule out to prove a set uncountable, and why is no bijection with N alone insufficient?
cards.definition: A set is uncountable when it is neither finite nor countably infinite. A sufficient obstruction is that no injection from it into N exists; for a nonempty set, showing that every proposed enumeration by N misses an element also suffices. Merely showing no bijection with N suffices only after establishing that the set is infinite. One failed candidate enumeration does not rule out all enumerations.
required_concepts: Uncountable excludes both finite and countably infinite sets.
The obstruction must apply to every possible enumeration or injection, not just one attempt.
No bijection with N requires an additional infinitude premise.
major_error_concepts: The singleton {0} is uncountable because there is no bijection N→{0}.

cards.prompt: Define Boundary-case analysis. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The deliberate test of empty singleton zero negative degenerate endpoint or smallest-size cases where hypotheses or constructions often change behavior.
required_concepts: The deliberate test of empty singleton zero negative degenerate endpoint or smallest-size cases where hypotheses or constructions often change behavior.
major_error_concepts: Treating boundary cases as unimportant because the generic algebra works later.

cards.prompt: Define Canonical and minimal examples. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The preference for the smallest structure exposing the decisive property or failure when size is part of explanatory power but not proof validity.
required_concepts: The preference for the smallest structure exposing the decisive property or failure when size is part of explanatory power but not proof validity.
major_error_concepts: Calling a large opaque example stronger without isolating the mechanism.

cards.prompt: Define Construction verification order. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The sequence that first types an object then proves totality or existence followed by each requested property and only then interprets the result.
required_concepts: The sequence that first types an object then proves totality or existence followed by each requested property and only then interprets the result.
major_error_concepts: Using later properties of an object that has not been shown well defined.

cards.prompt: What are the preconditions and decisive move in counterexample search by negation?
cards.definition: **Definition.** The method translating a universal claim's exact negation into construction constraints for an admissible falsifying object.
required_concepts: Begin with a universal claim and write its exact existential negation.
Use the negated predicate and domain restrictions as constraints on an admissible falsifying object.
major_error_concepts: Trying random examples without deriving the failure requirements.

cards.prompt: Define Definition and lemma citation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The exact attribution of an inference to an unfolded definition established lemma or theorem whose hypotheses are verified locally.
required_concepts: The exact attribution of an inference to an unfolded definition established lemma or theorem whose hypotheses are verified locally.
major_error_concepts: Writing clearly or obviously where a nontrivial dependency is needed.

cards.prompt: Define Example witness. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A concrete admissible object satisfying every clause of a specified property and used to establish possibility or illuminate a definition.
required_concepts: A concrete admissible object satisfying every clause of a specified property and used to establish possibility or illuminate a definition.
major_error_concepts: Offering an object without checking all clauses.

cards.prompt: Define False-converse diagnostic. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The construction of a case satisfying a theorem conclusion while its hypothesis fails to show the converse is not implied.
required_concepts: The construction of a case satisfying a theorem conclusion while its hypothesis fails to show the converse is not implied.
major_error_concepts: Refuting the original true implication instead of the reversed claim.

cards.prompt: Define Intuition proof and formalization distinction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The separation among motivating picture valid informal argument formal statement accepted proof term and kernel-checked artifact.
required_concepts: The separation among motivating picture valid informal argument formal statement accepted proof term and kernel-checked artifact.
major_error_concepts: Calling a persuasive diagram a proof or a parsed theorem a checked proof.

cards.prompt: Define Load-bearing proof prose. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The writing standard that every sentence introduces an object states a goal invokes a justified fact or advances the argument under exact references.
required_concepts: The writing standard that every sentence introduces an object states a goal invokes a justified fact or advances the argument under exact references.
major_error_concepts: Equating length or formality with rigor while irrelevant steps remain.

cards.prompt: Define Mathematical notation declaration. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The local introduction of symbols domains indices and conventions before use so every expression is typed and reconstructable.
required_concepts: The local introduction of symbols domains indices and conventions before use so every expression is typed and reconstructable.
major_error_concepts: Using i n and x before declaring their roles or domains.

cards.prompt: Define Missing-hypothesis diagnosis. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The use of a counterexample to identify which absent domain closure finiteness nonzero injectivity or other condition makes a proposed theorem false.
required_concepts: The use of a counterexample to identify which absent domain closure finiteness nonzero injectivity or other condition makes a proposed theorem false.
major_error_concepts: Adding an arbitrary condition that excludes the example but does not support a proof.

cards.prompt: Define Nonexample certificate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** A concrete admissible object failing a named decisive clause with the failure witness retained.
required_concepts: A concrete admissible object failing a named decisive clause with the failure witness retained.
major_error_concepts: Calling an object a nonexample without identifying the failed definition clause.

cards.prompt: Define Proof compression and expansion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The reversible movement between a concise expert proof and an explicit dependency version without deleting necessary hypotheses or inference steps.
required_concepts: The reversible movement between a concise expert proof and an explicit dependency version without deleting necessary hypotheses or inference steps.
major_error_concepts: Treating omitted decisive reasoning as harmless brevity.

cards.prompt: Define Proof error taxonomy. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The classification of domain mismatch unbound variable false premise invalid inference circularity incomplete cases bad witness representative dependence theorem misapplication and conclusion overreach.
required_concepts: Statement errors include a domain mismatch or an unbound variable.
Dependency errors include a false premise, invalid inference, or circularity.
Coverage errors include incomplete cases or an invalid witness.
Structural errors include representative dependence, theorem misapplication, or conclusion overreach.
major_error_concepts: Calling every failure a minor algebra mistake.

cards.prompt: Define Scope of a mathematical conclusion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The scope of a mathematical conclusion is the exact domain, hypotheses, and logical strength for which the proof establishes its claim; stronger generality, effective construction, or a converse requires additional argument.
required_concepts: Retain the proved domain and every hypothesis.
State only the conclusion's proved logical strength.
A converse, stronger generality, or effective construction needs additional argument.
major_error_concepts: Dropping a hypothesis, enlarging the domain, asserting a converse, or claiming an effective construction when the proof established only existence.

cards.prompt: Define Theorem repair. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The minimal or principled revision of hypotheses domain or conclusion that removes the counterexample and admits a new proof.
required_concepts: The minimal or principled revision of hypotheses domain or conclusion that removes the counterexample and admits a new proof.
major_error_concepts: Deleting the hard case or weakening the conclusion until it becomes vacuous.

cards.prompt: Define Variable-scope discipline. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
cards.definition: **Definition.** The control of arbitrary chosen existential and locally defined variables so witness ownership and dependencies remain visible.
required_concepts: The control of arbitrary chosen existential and locally defined variables so witness ownership and dependencies remain visible.
major_error_concepts: Reusing a symbol with a new meaning or letting a local witness escape its scope.

description: A definition-recall course deck covering core concepts in Introduction to Mathematical Proofs.
